Identity, Civil Registration, Police & Legal Services | Bangladesh
Verified cut-off: 25 October 2026
1. How to use this file in JANUN
Each service record contains only verified facts, the main official source URL, and additional official references.
Dynamic fields such as fees, local requirements and processing times should keep a last_verified_at date in the app.
For location-dependent certificates, JANUN must ask the user’s local authority before showing a fixed checklist or fee.
QR/source cards in Appendix A are visual source references, not screenshots of private user data.

3. Data intentionally NOT included as verified facts
Exact nationwide BDRIS birth/death correction or reprint fees where the current official fee table was not reliably captured.
One fixed nationwide processing time for registrar-based birth/death corrections.
One fixed national fee/document checklist for citizenship, permanent-resident and heir certificates; these vary by local authority.
One exact nationwide marriage/divorce registration fee in the current portal where a current official citizen fee schedule was not confirmed.
One fixed nationwide Notary Public/affidavit fee.
One universal “name change” workflow covering Birth Registration, NID, passport and academic records - each authority has a separate process.

tables.text: Verification rule used in this edition: Only facts supported by an official Government of Bangladesh portal, law, official notice, citizen charter, or official manual are included. Unverified nationwide fees, processing times, and local-document checklists are intentionally excluded.
Office of Registrar General, Birth & Death Registration / local registrar
BDRIS provides the official online birth-registration application.
The ORGBDR citizen charter instructs birth registration within 45 days of birth.
The application collects child, parent and address information and accepts supporting image attachments.
BDRIS has a dedicated birth-information correction service.
The applicant must identify the existing record and submit documentary evidence supporting the requested correction.
Registrar review/decision is required; approval is not automatic.
Name, date of birth and parent-data corrections are handled through the official BDRIS correction route.
Supporting evidence is required for the field being corrected.
The corrected civil record should be used before updating dependent identity documents.
Official birth-record verification uses the 17-digit birth registration number and date of birth.
Verification is available through the government eVerify service.
Reprint services are accessed through BDRIS/local registrar workflow.
BDRIS provides the official online death-registration application.
ORGBDR citizen guidance instructs death registration within 45 days.
Death-record correction is handled through the official BDRIS framework.
This is the Election Commission/NID Wing citizen portal for NID-related online services.
Citizens can use it for account-based NID services including registration/correction/reissue workflows where available.
The NID portal includes the official route for new registration.
Election Commission publishes the prescribed national identity registration forms and field-office Citizen Charter.
Applicants must provide identity/civil-registration and address evidence according to the current EC process.
NID correction requires supporting evidence for the specific field.
EC guidance lists records such as SSC certificate, birth registration, passport, driving licence, marriage/divorce documents, affidavit/newspaper notice or service book depending on the case.
2026 EC fee notice: visible NID data correction - 1st Tk 200 + VAT 30; 2nd Tk 300 + VAT 45; later Tk 400 + VAT 60.
2026 EC fee notice: other stored information correction - 1st Tk 100 + VAT 15; 2nd Tk 200 + VAT 30; later Tk 300 + VAT 45.
Election Commission publishes the official reissue/duplicate route and forms.
2026 EC fee notice: normal duplicate - 1st Tk 200, 2nd Tk 300, subsequent Tk 500; 15% VAT applies.
2026 EC fee notice: urgent duplicate - 1st Tk 300, 2nd Tk 500, subsequent Tk 1000; 15% VAT applies.
Citizens use the NID portal for their own account/service information.
Election Commission publishes separate prescribed forms for formal verification/data-supply workflows.
Public users should not be told that they can freely query another person’s NID data.
Local Government authority / Prottoyon where covered
Prottoyon is a government-backed online citizen-certificate platform used by covered local authorities.
Citizen profile and address information are used for certificate applications.
Certificate availability depends on whether the relevant Union/Municipality/local authority is covered.
Marriage.gov.bd is the official Marriage & Divorce Registration System.
For Muslim marriages, the Muslim Marriages and Divorces (Registration) Act 1974 requires registration.
If a Muslim marriage is solemnized by someone other than the Nikah Registrar, the bridegroom must report it to the concerned Nikah Registrar within 30 days.
The portal provides citizen registration using identity information.
Nikah Registrar / local Chairman / court as applicable
Under section 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961, after pronouncing talaq the husband must give written notice to the Chairman and a copy to the wife.
Talaq generally does not become effective until 90 days after delivery of notice to the Chairman, subject to the statutory pregnancy rule.
The Chairman constitutes an Arbitration Council within 30 days to attempt reconciliation.
Divorce registration by Nikah Registrar is governed by section 6 of the 1974 registration law.
Prottoyon supports ওয়ারিশ/উত্তরাধিকার certificate services in covered local authorities.
Applicant registration uses mobile number and identity information; local authority approval is required.
Prottoyon has an official integration notice relating online heir-certificate verification with e-Mutation.
There is no single government service that changes a person’s name across every record at once.
Birth-record correction uses BDRIS; NID correction uses the Election Commission/NID process.
Supporting evidence requirements depend on the target document and type of change.
Dependent records should be updated after the foundational record is corrected.
Bangladesh Police provides the official online PCC portal.
The portal requires an online application, passport/address documentation and fee-payment proof according to applicant type.
Current portal fee: Tk 1,500 via Treasury Challan/online payment plus applicable service charge.
Status SMS format shown by portal: PCC S <reference> to 26969.
Bangladesh Police provides the official Online GD system.
Citizens submit identity/contact, incident/lost-item details and supporting evidence where available.
The official user manual explains account/application workflow.
For immediate danger/emergency, use 999 rather than a routine GD.
Online GD supports reporting lost documents/items.
Users provide item/document identifying details, place/time/circumstances and supporting evidence where available.
The acknowledgement/reference can be used in subsequent replacement processes where the receiving authority requires it.
Notary / MOFA / issuing authority depending on use
The Notaries Ordinance authorizes notaries to verify, authenticate, certify or attest instruments and perform other statutory functions.
For documents for foreign use, the appropriate MOFA/e-Consular or mission route depends on the document and destination.
For government-issued records, use the issuing authority’s own verification system when available.
Notaries are governed by the Notaries Ordinance 1961.
A notary may authenticate/certify/attest instruments, administer oaths and take affidavits within statutory authority.
A receiving authority may or may not require an affidavit; JANUN should only recommend it when the target authority requires it.
Government legal aid is available under the Legal Aid Services Act 2000 (as amended) for eligible justice-seekers.
Applications can be made through the official online system or prescribed LA Form-01/district legal-aid office.
The application collects applicant, income/occupation, case/dispute and supporting-document information.
GRS is the official government grievance system for complaints about government service delivery.
Citizens can lodge a complaint by selecting office/service/location, describing the grievance and attaching evidence.
The current complaint form allows evidence attachments up to 10 MB in supported formats.
GRS provides appeal/escalation mechanisms under its guideline.
BDRIS / Election Commission / other issuing authority
The correction route depends on which foundational record is wrong.
If the birth record is wrong, use BDRIS correction.
If NID is wrong while the foundational civil record is correct, use the EC/NID correction process with supporting evidence.
After the foundational record is corrected, dependent documents should be updated with their issuing authorities.
